Les données contenues dans ces supports et documents sont strictement couvertes par le secret professionnel (article 226-13 du code pénal). Conformément aux articles 34 et 35 de la loi du 6 janvier 1978 modifiée relative à l’informatique, aux fichiers et aux libertés, le titulaire du présent accord-cadre s’engage à prendre toutes précautions utiles afin de préserver la sécurité des informations et notamment d’empêcher qu’elles ne soient déformées, endommagées ou communiquées à des personnes non autorisées. Le titulaire s’engage donc à respecter, de façon absolue, les obligations suivantes et à les faire respecter par son personnel, c’est-à-dire notamment à : Ne prendre aucune copie des documents et supports d’informations confiés, à l’exception de celles nécessaires pour les besoins de l’exécution de sa prestation, objet du présent accord-cadre Ne pas utiliser les documents et informations traités à des fins autres que celles spécifiées au présent accord-cadre Ne pas divulgue

DUME Bien que son utilisation ne soit pas obligatoire, l’Ined encourage fortement les candidats à renseigner un Document Unique de Marché Européen (DUME) pour candidater. 1.1. Qu’est-ce que le DUME Le DUME est un formulaire électronique standardisé qui permet à un opérateur économique de présenter sa candidature à un marché public en déclarant son identité, sa situation juridique, financière et ses capacités professionnelles. Il est accessible en ligne, notamment via la plateforme https://dume.chorus -pro.gouv.fr ou directement depuis certains profils acheteurs sur https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr. Grâce à ce formulaire, l’entreprise peut bénéficier d’un pré remplissage automatique de certaines informations à partir de son numéro SIRET, ce qui réduit le nombre de saisies. references_experience.text: Tout manquement sera sanctionné. Les produits échantillonnés devront être présentés tels qu’ils seront livrés en cours d’exécution du marché. Les étiquettes de chaque échantillon devront être conformes aux exigences du présent marché. Au cas où il existerait un désaccord entre les spécifications annoncées et celles relevées sur les échantillons, c'est toujours la formule la plus avantageuse pour le client qui sera retenue pour devenir base contractuelle du marché. Les cartons de livraison porteront obligatoirement le nom du candidat avec la mention « ECHANTILLONS MARCHE CROUS ». Il sera accompagné d’un bon de livraison détaillé précisant la référence et/ou la marque de chaque produit, ainsi que les fiches techniques de l’ensemble des échantillons. Le défaut de présentation des documents exigés (étiquettes, bon de livraison, fiches techniques) entraînera également le rejet de l’offre. Il est rappelé que les échantillons demandés, ainsi que les précisions apportées dans l'offre par les fiches techniques, constitueront la définition contractuelle des produits retenus. Tous les échantillons remis par les candidats, retenus ou non, restent acquis à l’établissement. is competition. Part 2: Overview of the Contracting Authority 2.1. About the RIA The Contracting Authority is the Royal Irish Academy (RIA). The RIA is an all -island learned society whose mission is to recognise and foster academic excellence and to create, curate and share knowledge for the benefit of society. The Academy’s activities include research programmes, grants and awards, scholarly publications, library and cultural heritage services, public engagement, facilities management and the operation of the Digital Repository of Ireland. These activities creat e a varied financial operating environment involving departmental budgets, externally funded projects, restricted funds, grants, procurement, stock, sales, subscriptions, donations and other income streams. The RIA requires reliable financial information to support management, budget holders, funders, auditors and other stakeholders. Bei Nutzung von Cloud-Diensten sind zusätzlich die gesetzlichen Vorgaben nach § 393 SGB V zur Verarbeitung von Sozial- und Gesundheitsdaten in der Cloud zu erfüllen. Our strategy sets a clear pathway to achieve net zero emissions in a way that supports our customers and ensures ESB’s continued growth. ESB are committed to leading the transition to a reliable and affordable net zero future. ESB seeks to purchase supplies, services and works that are produced or delivered in a manner that has the most positive environmental, social and economic impacts possible over their entire lifecycle. ESB procurement processes will be aligned with the standards from ISO20400, Sustainable Procurement. ESB have created a Sustainability Leadership Plan which sets out our ambitions and the actions we will take as they relate to the three pillars of sustainability - People, Planet and Place. Full details of ESB’s Sustainability Leadership Plan can be viewed here: ESB Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB requires that the successful Contractor emerging from the Procurement process be familiar with our Sustainable Leadership Plan. ESB is a founding member of the Irish Supply Chain Sustainability School. The school’s aim is to support and develop skills and knowledge in sustainability in the built environment. Further

As a strong, diversified, vertically integrated utility, ESB operates right across the electricity market: from generation, through transmission and distribution, to supply. In addition, ESB extracts further value at certain points along this chain: supplying gas, using our networks to carry fibre for telecommunications, developing electric vehicle public charging infrastructure and more. ESB is a leading Irish utility focused on providing excellent customer service and maintaining our financial strength. We have a regulated asset base of approximately €12 billion with 30% of electricity generation capacity in the all-island market. We currently supply electricity to approximately 2.5 million customers throughout the island of Ireland. ESB Group employs approximately 10,000 people. Protecting our environment is a huge responsibility, and we work with a number of organisations that carry out specific environmental functions. All respondents in the digital industry study pointed to the availability of skilled labour as a crucial factor behind their decision to launch an investment in Lower Silesia20. PRODUCT PERSONALISATION AND SERVITISATION The ability to create more product variants while using the same resources is crucial to building a competitive advantage. That’s why increasing production flexibility has long been a pressing matter for manufacturers. Again, data is the game-changer here. Processing real-time information at all stages of user interactions enables creating product simulations that can be adapted to match unique, individual requirements of the customer. Similarly, many manufacturing businesses now expand the value for their clients by shifting from selling products to selling Product-Service Systems (PSS). Pioneered in the 1960s by Rolls Royce, servitisation relieves customers of capital costs, instead offering them advanced solutions in a subscription model. 16 PLATFORMISATION OF PRODUCTION Just as products are now increasingly offered as a service, the manufacturing process is also subject to similar changes. ON INDUSTRY 4.0 WORLDWIDE Before the outbreak of COVID-19, there was widespread interest in Industry 4.0. The sector’s value was projected to grow up to $3.7 trillion by 20259. However, despite these positive outlooks, the actual landscape of Industry 4.0 adoption has been far more complex. ASPIRATIONS VS REALITY 90% of respondents in McKinsey’s10 annual survey admitted seeing the benefits of digital transformation in manufacturing. A majority of them included introducing new technologies as an essential part of their organisational development strategies. However, as research from the World Economic Forum11 demonstrates, despite these declarations, the reality was still far from this ideal. In 2018, the adoption of technology in production still remained slow across industries and regions. ip_data_security.text: This change wouldn’t be possible without advancements such as the Internet of Things (IoT), the Cloud, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), or Artificial Intelligence (AI). 13 Therefore, this publication follows the BCG’s definition of Industry 4.01, seeing it as a transformation that enables analysing data across machines and using it for more efficient manufacturing at reduced costs. CORE TECHNOLOGIES SUPPORTING INDUSTRY 4.0 Autonomous robots & cobots Digital Twins & simulation The AI-powered cloud Augmented & virtual reality Digital integration systems The Industrial Internet of Things Additive manufacturing Big Data & analytics Cybersecurity * ORGANISED AFTER THE BOSTON CONSUL TING GROUP Apart from increasing productivity, Industry 4.0 also encourages developing new products and business models. As a result, it modifies the workforce profile and reconfigures the competitiveness of companies and regions. These issues will be discussed later on in this chapter but first, let’s focus on the three core advancements differentiating Industry 4.0 from the previous revolutions. DATIFICATION Integrating data from devices, sensors, and IT systems enables developing new solutions at all stages of the product lifecycle – from design to production, logistics and maintenance. 1

ntinuously collecting, analysing, and using data in real-time. IIoT enables monitoring of all production processes and scheduling maintenance accordingly. When integrating Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Customer Relationship Management (CRM), the network allows for comprehensive management of all related operations. THE CONVERGENCE OF IT SYSTEMS AND OPERATIONAL TECHNOLOGY (OT) In the past, IT and OT worked as separate entities: the first one mostly serving management, the latter controlling machines and resources. Thanks to the IIoT, these two worlds have been increasingly converging. Cyber-physical systems (CPS) embody this tendency as machines now combine both the IT and operational qualities. One of the most advanced CP systems – Digital Twins – enables creating digital replicas of physical objects but also processes based on data collected from sensors. ROBOTISATION AND AUTOMATION Industry 4.0 is also underpinned by a growing level of robotisation and automation. Apart from automated production lines, factories now boast autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and collaborative robots (cobots). The Specialist will manage relationships with regional research partners, research teams, and technical consultants, ensuring that all regional public goods and knowledge assets align seamlessly with country demands.

For the avoidance of doubt, the final Systems Audit Report shall be submitted not later than six (6) months following the end of the financial year under review. The Systems Audit shall include, but not be limited to, a review of the billing system environment, billing processes and controls, user access management, segregation of duties, data integrity, billing accuracy, tariff configuration controls, customer account management controls, billing adjustments and exception handling procedures, revenue assurance controls, interface controls between systems, audit trails, change management procedures, reporting controls, business continuity arrangements, backup and recovery procedures, and compliance with applicable policies, procedures and regulatory requirements. The Contractor shall assess the adequacy, effectiveness and reliability of the controls in place and identify any weaknesses, risks or areas for improvement. The Contractor shall submit a Systems Audit Report detailing findings, risks, recommendations, proposed corrective actions and, where appropriate, prioritisation of recommendations based on their significance and potential impact. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

Στο αντικείμενο της σύμβασης περιλαμβάνεται η παροχή της απαιτούμενης υποδομής VMware, των αναγκαίων υπολογιστικών, αποθηκευτικών και δικτυακών πόρων, καθώς και η εγκατάσταση, παραμετροποίηση και λειτουργία της υπηρεσίας Disaster Recovery. Οι τεχνικές προδιαγραφές τόσο του Κέντρου Δεδομένων όσο και των υπηρεσιών περιγράφονται στο Έντυπο 9 - ΠΙΝΑΚΑΣ ΠΡΟΣΦΟΡΑΣ ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΜΟΡΦΩΣΗΣ. Η λύση θα υποστηρίζει τη συνεχή αναπαραγωγή (replication) των επιλεγμένων εικονικών μηχανών του Πανεπιστημίου προς το περιβάλλον του Αναδόχου, με χρήση του λογισμικού Veeam Backup and Replication, ώστε να διασφαλίζεται η δυνατότητα ανάκτησης των κρίσιμων πληροφοριακών συστημάτων σε περίπτωση σοβαρής διακοπής λειτουργίας ή καταστροφής του κύριου Κέντρου Δεδομένων του Πανεπιστημίου Κύπρου. Στόχος είναι η συνέχιση της παροχής υπηρεσιών μέσω διαδικτύου προς την Πανεπιστημιακή κοινότητα και το κοινό, με τον ελάχιστο δυνατό χρόνο διακοπής. Η λύση θα πρέπει να παρέχει τη δυνατότητα ενεργοποίησης (failover) των επιλεγμένων εικονικών μηχανών στο περιβάλλον του Αναδόχου όταν και εφόσον κριθεί αναγκαίο, καθώς και δυνατότητα ασφαλούς επαναφοράς (failback) στο κύριο Κέντρο Δεδομένων του Πανεπιστημίου μετά την αποκατάσταση

ουσας Αρχής. Κατά τη διάρκεια της επίσκεψης, τα άτομα της Αναθέτουσας Αρχής θα έχουν συναντήσεις με τους αρμόδιους μηχανικούς του DR Datacenter και θα παρουσιαστούν η υποδομή και η αρχιτεκτονική του χώρου, οι μηχανισμοί πλεονασμού και διαθεσιμότητας, καθώς και οι διαδικασίες Disaster Recovery. Παράλληλα, θα παρουσιαστούν οι διαδικασίες replication, failover/failback και αποκατάστασης των συστημάτων σε περίπτωση καταστροφής ή διακοπής λειτουργίας. Ο Ανάδοχος πρέπει να συμπεριλάβει στην προσφορά του όλα τα τυχών έξοδα για την επίσκεψη (κόστος μεταφοράς, διαμονής, γεύματα κτλ.). Υφιστάμενη Υποδομή 1.3.1 Εικονική Υποδομή Η υφιστάμενη εικονική υποδομή VMware του ΠΚ αποτελείται από 2 ξεχωριστά clusters, τα οποία φιλοξενούνται σε 2 Κέντρα Δεδομένων εγκατεστημένα σε διαφορετικές τοποθεσίες στη Λευκωσία. Για την προστασία των εικονικών μηχανών και των φυσικών εξυπηρετητών χρησιμοποιείται η λύση Veeam Backup and Replication η οποία παρέχει υπηρεσίες δημιουργίας αντιγράφων ασφαλείας και αποκατάστασης δεδομένων. L’intervention des cordistes est interdite et nécessite l’utilisation d’une nacelle automotrice pilotée par des personnels certifiés munis de moyens de protection individuelle normalisés. (Voir article “ Etablissement des Plans de prévention des risques”) La méthode de pose est la s

isée suivant les mesures de prévention indiqué au plan de prévention, à l’écart de la circulation du public. La pose de filets de protection n’est pas nécessaire. Il est nécessaire de formuler la demande de déplacement du module de lavage 8 jours ouvrables avant la date d’intervention, au responsable du marché. La bâche BO.3 se fixe depuis une nacelle de 60 m stationnée sur la Piazza Pompidou, dans une zone à baliser et à surveiller strictement. La pose d’un filet de protection ou replis de la bâche existante est indispensable sur la chenille en verre pour protection. Le montant de l'avance est fixé à 5,00 % du montant du bon de commande si la durée de son exécution est inférieure ou égale à douze mois ; si cette durée est supérieure à douze mois, l'avance est égale à 5,00 % d'une somme égale à douze fois le montant du bon de commande divisé par cette durée exprimée en mois. Le remboursement de l'avance commence lorsque le montant des prestations exécutées par le titulaire atteint ou dépasse 65,00 % de la part du montant toutes taxes comprises du bon de commande exécutée par le titulaire. Il doit être terminé lorsque ledit montant atteint 80,00 %. Ce remboursement s'effectue par précompte sur

ivisé par cette durée exprimée en mois. Le remboursement de l'avance commence lorsque le montant des prestations exécutées par le titulaire atteint ou dépasse 65,00 % de la part du montant toutes taxes comprises du bon de commande exécutée par le titulaire. Il doit être terminé lorsque ledit montant atteint 80,00 %. Ce remboursement s'effectue par précompte sur les sommes dues ultérieurement au titulaire à titre d'acompte ou de solde. En cas de groupement d'opérateurs économiques, la part de l'avance est rapportée au montant des prestations individualisées par membre. A défaut, l'avance est versée sur le compte du groupement ou du mandataire qui aura la charge de la répartir entre les m embres du groupement. Une avance peut être versée, sur leur demande, aux sous -traitants bénéficiaires du paiement direct suivant les mêmes dispositions que celles applicables au titulaire de l'accord-cadre, avec les particularités détaillées aux articles R. 2191-6, R. 2193-10 et R. 2193-17 à R. 2193-21 du Code de la commande publique. 8.2 - Garanties financières de l'avance Aucune garantie financière ne sera demandée au titulaire pour le versement de l'avance. Dans ce dernier cas, un dossier de consultation (comprenant un acte d’engagement, un cahier des clauses particulières et une lettre de consultation) sera adressé au titulaire de l’accord -cadre précisant les caractéristiques et les modalités d’exécution des prestations demandées. Qu’est-ce que le DUME Le DUME est un formulaire électronique standardisé qui permet à un opérateur économique de présenter sa candidature à un marché public en déclarant son identité, sa situation juridique, financière et ses capacités professionnelles. Il est accessible en ligne, notamment via la plateforme https://dume.chorus -pro.gouv.fr ou directement depuis certains profils acheteurs sur https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr. Grâce à ce formulaire, l’entreprise peut bénéficier d’un pré remplissage automatique de certaines informations à partir de son numéro SIRET, ce qui réduit le nombre de saisies. references_experience.text: Tout manquement sera sanctionné. Les produits échantillonnés devront être présentés tels qu’ils seront livrés en cours d’exécution du marché. Les étiquettes de chaque échantillon devront être conformes aux exigences du présent marché. Les cartons de livraison porteront obligatoirement le nom du candidat avec la mention « ECHANTILLONS MARCHE CROUS ». Il sera accompagné d’un bon de livraison détaillé précisant la référence et/ou la marque de chaque produit, ainsi que les fiches techniques de l’ensemble des échantillons. Le défaut de présentation des documents exigés (étiquettes, bon de livraison, fiches techniques) entraînera également le rejet de l’offre. Il est rappelé que les échantillons demandés, ainsi que les précisions apportées dans l'offre par les fiches techniques, constitueront la définition contractuelle des produits retenus. Tous les échantillons remis par les candidats, retenus ou non, restent acquis à l’établissement. Protecting our environment is a huge responsibility, and we work with a number of organisations that carry out specific environmental functions. As of August 2014, we are also responsible for ensuring that the people of Ireland are protected from the harmful effects of radiation. ON INDUSTRY 4.0 WORLDWIDE Before the outbreak of COVID-19, there was widespread interest in Industry 4.0. The sector’s value was projected to grow up to $3.7 trillion by 20259. However, despite these positive outlooks, the actual landscape of Industry 4.0 adoption has been far more complex. ASPIRATIONS VS REALITY 90% of respondents in McKinsey’s10 annual survey admitted seeing the benefits of digital transformation in manufacturing. A majority of them included introducing new technologies as an essential part of their organisational development strategies. However, as research from the World Economic Forum11 demonstrates, despite these declarations, the reality was still far from this ideal. In 2018, the adoption of technology in production still remained slow across industries and regions. CORE TECHNOLOGIES SUPPORTING INDUSTRY 4.0 Autonomous robots & cobots Digital Twins & simulation The AI-powered cloud Augmented & virtual reality Digital integration systems The Industrial Internet of Things Additive manufacturing Big Data & analytics Cybersecurity * ORGANISED AFTER THE BOSTON CONSUL TING GROUP Apart from increasing productivity, Industry 4.0 also encourages developing new products and business models. As a result, it modifies the workforce profile and reconfigures the competitiveness of companies and regions. These issues will be discussed later on in this chapter but first, let’s focus on the three core advancements differentiating Industry 4.0 from the previous revolutions. DATIFICATION Integrating data from devices, sensors, and IT systems enables developing new solutions at all stages of the product lifecycle – from design to production, logistics and maintenance. 1

ntinuously collecting, analysing, and using data in real-time. IIoT enables monitoring of all production processes and scheduling maintenance accordingly. When integrating Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Customer Relationship Management (CRM), the network allows for comprehensive management of all related operations. THE CONVERGENCE OF IT SYSTEMS AND OPERATIONAL TECHNOLOGY (OT) In the past, IT and OT worked as separate entities: the first one mostly serving management, the latter controlling machines and resources. Thanks to the IIoT, these two worlds have been increasingly converging. Cyber-physical systems (CPS) embody this tendency as machines now combine both the IT and operational qualities. One of the most advanced CP systems – Digital Twins – enables creating digital replicas of physical objects but also processes based on data collected from sensors. ROBOTISATION AND AUTOMATION Industry 4.0 is also underpinned by a growing level of robotisation and automation. Apart from automated production lines, factories now boast autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and collaborative robots (cobots). Website Hosting & Support Service The objective of this tender process is to invite proposals for the provision of website hosting, ongoing maintenance and development services for the CORU website. Tenderers shall demonstrate their capability to provide a secure, reliable, and resilient hosting environment that supports the continued availability and performance of the website. Particular consideration will be given to: • The location of the hosting infrastructure and the suitability of the hosting arrangement from a regulatory, operational, and data governance perspective. • The provision of secure and user -friendly content management functionality that enables authorised CORU staff to undertake routine and moderate website content updates without requiring specialist technical support. • The implementation of appropriate security controls, monitoring, and maintenance processes to protect the website from unauthorised access, modification, disruption, or malicious activi

Website Migration Services The successful tenderer shall be responsible for the migration of CORU's existing live website to the proposed hosting environment. The migration service shall include, at a minimum: • Development and execution of a detailed migration plan, including timelines, responsibilities, testing and implementation activities. • Migration of all website content, functionality, configurations and associated assets to the proposed environment. • Measures to minimise disruption to website availability and user experience during the migration process. • Comprehensive testing prior to go -live, including functional, security, performance, accessibility and user acceptance testing. • Provision of rollback and recovery procedures in the event of migration issues. • Preservation of existing search engine rankings and implementation of any necessary redirects and SEO protections during migration. • Post-migration support to address any issues arising following implementation. The proposed hosting solution shall: • Be hosted within the European Union, with hosting in Ireland preferred. • Be secure, resilient and scalable. • Support high availability and business continuity requirements. For the avoidance of doubt, the final Systems Audit Report shall be submitted not later than six (6) months following the end of the financial year under review. The Systems Audit shall include, but not be limited to, a review of the billing system environment, billing processes and controls, user access management, segregation of duties, data integrity, billing accuracy, tariff configuration controls, customer account management controls, billing adjustments and exception handling procedures, revenue assurance controls, interface controls between systems, audit trails, change management procedures, reporting controls, business continuity arrangements, backup and recovery procedures, and compliance with applicable policies, procedures and regulatory requirements. The Contractor shall assess the adequacy, effectiveness and reliability of the controls in place and identify any weaknesses, risks or areas for improvement. The Contractor shall submit a Systems Audit Report detailing findings, risks, recommendations, proposed corrective actions and, where appropriate, prioritisation of recommendations based on their significance and potential impact. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

Στο αντικείμενο της σύμβασης περιλαμβάνεται η παροχή της απαιτούμενης υποδομής VMware, των αναγκαίων υπολογιστικών, αποθηκευτικών και δικτυακών πόρων, καθώς και η εγκατάσταση, παραμετροποίηση και λειτουργία της υπηρεσίας Disaster Recovery. Οι τεχνικές προδιαγραφές τόσο του Κέντρου Δεδομένων όσο και των υπηρεσιών περιγράφονται στο Έντυπο 9 - ΠΙΝΑΚΑΣ ΠΡΟΣΦΟΡΑΣ ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΜΟΡΦΩΣΗΣ. Η λύση θα υποστηρίζει τη συνεχή αναπαραγωγή (replication) των επιλεγμένων εικονικών μηχανών του Πανεπιστημίου προς το περιβάλλον του Αναδόχου, με χρήση του λογισμικού Veeam Backup and Replication, ώστε να διασφαλίζεται η δυνατότητα ανάκτησης των κρίσιμων πληροφοριακών συστημάτων σε περίπτωση σοβαρής διακοπής λειτουργίας ή καταστροφής του κύριου Κέντρου Δεδομένων του Πανεπιστημίου Κύπρου. Στόχος είναι η συνέχιση της παροχής υπηρεσιών μέσω διαδικτύου προς την Πανεπιστημιακή κοινότητα και το κοινό, με τον ελάχιστο δυνατό χρόνο διακοπής. Η λύση θα πρέπει να παρέχει τη δυνατότητα ενεργοποίησης (failover) των επιλεγμένων εικονικών μηχανών στο περιβάλλον του Αναδόχου όταν και εφόσον κριθεί αναγκαίο, καθώς και δυνατότητα ασφαλούς επαναφοράς (failback) στο κύριο Κέντρο Δεδομένων του Πανεπιστημίου μετά την αποκατάσταση

ουσας Αρχής. Κατά τη διάρκεια της επίσκεψης, τα άτομα της Αναθέτουσας Αρχής θα έχουν συναντήσεις με τους αρμόδιους μηχανικούς του DR Datacenter και θα παρουσιαστούν η υποδομή και η αρχιτεκτονική του χώρου, οι μηχανισμοί πλεονασμού και διαθεσιμότητας, καθώς και οι διαδικασίες Disaster Recovery. Παράλληλα, θα παρουσιαστούν οι διαδικασίες replication, failover/failback και αποκατάστασης των συστημάτων σε περίπτωση καταστροφής ή διακοπής λειτουργίας. Ο Ανάδοχος πρέπει να συμπεριλάβει στην προσφορά του όλα τα τυχών έξοδα για την επίσκεψη (κόστος μεταφοράς, διαμονής, γεύματα κτλ.). Υλοποίηση της αρχικής αντιγραφής των δεδομένων και των επιλεγμένων εικονικών μηχανών από το κύριο κέντρο δεδομένων προς το περιβάλλον DR. Περιλαμβάνεται η ρύθμιση των μηχανισμών replication, ο έλεγχος της ορθής μεταφοράς των δεδομένων και λειτουργίας και η επιβεβαίωση της ετοιμότητας του περιβάλλοντος για ενεργοποίηση σε περίπτωση καταστροφής.
